scope: Twelve current numbered additions: six finite-group/matrix statements, five main controlled-process statements and one supplement approximation theorem. This is an inventory, not twelve claims of new classical theory.

source_verification.scope: Identity, catalog, label and declared dependency consistency; not a proof checker, native build or priority clearance.

statements.claim_class: Classical representation-theoretic mechanism stated and proved in the precise multi-output conventions required here; not a claim to invent Fourier decomposition or real descent.
classical_ingredients: Complete reducibility and finite group-algebra decomposition
A nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots
statements.conclusion: The multiplicity of rho in V_b complexified is rank A_rho(b); the trivial multiplicity is one. A real equivariant injection exists exactly when all complex irreducible multiplicities are dominated, including complex and quaternionic real types.
hypotheses: A finite group G, a finite nonempty output set C, and a probability table b:G->Delta(C); the action on the table need not be faithful.
All output Fourier matrices are stacked vertically, and V_b is the real cyclic span of the left translates.
For the descent assertion, U and V are arbitrary finite-dimensional real G-modules.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: lem:r75-fourier-multiplicity
statements.limits: A linear multiplicity criterion alone is not a positive factorization. The next theorem separately proves stochastic positivity.
statements.proof: Classical Fourier decomposition identifies the rho cyclic block with {A_rho M}, which has rank(A_rho) row copies. A complex injection A+iB descends because a nonzero maximal minor of A+zB is a real polynomial nonzero at i and therefore at some real z; the degree bound gives a finite candidate list.

statements.claim_class: Exact action-restricted resource count and its unrestricted multiplicity-cover form. The positivity mechanism extends the retained R74 construction and is reproduced explicitly.
classical_ingredients: Invariant inner products and complete reducibility
Positivity by mixing with a strictly positive average
statements.conclusion: For every positive contrast, q_H(b_t)>=max_rho ceil(r_rho/m_rho(H)); this is attained on an explicit positive interval whenever finite. The integer multiplicity cover gives the exact permutation-module minimum and the unrestricted positive core at sufficiently small positive contrast.
hypotheses: Finite G and C, b:G->Delta(C), group mean pi, and b_t=pi+t(b-pi), 0<=t<=1.
For the restricted count, a prescribed subgroup H and disjoint copies of H\G; missing active irreducible types give infinite copy number.
For the unrestricted cover, one representative of every subgroup conjugacy class; the pure-start formula is applied only when G is the observable group.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: thm:r75-orbit-multiplicity
statements.limits: Small positive contrast only for matching general synthesis; q_H is not kappa/[G:H] in general. At t=0 one copy suffices. No arbitrary full-contrast nonnormal-group LP is asserted.
statements.proof: Semisimplicity embeds the response subquotient in every realizing permutation module. Frobenius reciprocity counts each coset orbit. A real embedding of the centered response, invariant orthogonal projection, a uniform preparation perturbation, and a bounded decoder perturbation give the matching positive factorization on any prescribed adequate action. Zero-mean output columns are restored as zero columns.

statements.claim_class: Necessary and sufficient convexity classification for a fixed transitive probability-response action, with an explicit positive-contrast obstruction.
classical_ingredients: Centrality of the subgroup average iff the subgroup is normal
statements.conclusion: The binary single-orbit response set is convex exactly when H is normal. In the nonnormal case the averaged return character witnesses failure at every positive contrast; an irreducible block with 0<m_rho(H)<d_rho gives sup-norm distance at least t*m_rho(H)/(d*d_rho).
hypotheses: A finite group G, subgroup H, and transitive right action X=H\G of degree d.
Binary terminal responses on exactly this one orbit, with arbitrary probability preparation and stochastic decoder; no additional hidden orbit or mixture label is supplied.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: thm:r75-normality-convexity
statements.limits: The displayed distance is a rigorous lower bound, not a claimed sharp distance for all actions. The result concerns the specified action and does not preclude other formulations or larger positive cores.
statements.proof: Normal H gives exactly all H-invariant probability tables by a point preparation. If H is nonnormal, its group-algebra averaging projection is noncentral, so some irreducible fixed-space rank is strictly between zero and full degree. The normalized permutation character has a full scalar Fourier block there, which a single orbit cannot carry. A kernel vector of every competing rank-deficient block yields the quantitative margin.

statements.claim_class: Elementary equality lemma used to certify the full-contrast endpoint; no separate broad novelty claim.
classical_ingredients: Equality in a convex combination of numbers bounded by one
Uniform averaging on a transitive action
statements.conclusion: Each active component has a point preparation and the matching point-indicator decoder, hence is a pure return law.
hypotheses: A finite mixture of positive-weight components on copies of one fixed transitive d-point G-action X, with probability preparations and scalar decoders in [0,1].
The mixed response has value one at the identity and uniform group average 1/d.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: lem:r75-return-rigidity
statements.limits: The common orbit degree and positive mixture weights are essential. The symmetric-group theorem separately excludes other orbit types before applying it.
statements.proof: Identity value one forces each decoder to equal one throughout its preparation support. Transitivity makes its group average the decoder average, at least 1/d. Equality of the mixture average forces support size one and zeros off that point in each active component.

statements.claim_class: Sharp inequality and complete equality classification proved in this revision for a nonsymmetric nonnegative singular-matrix class. This is an author claim with a full elementary proof, not an exhaustive priority certificate.
classical_ingredients: A concave quadratic attains its minimum at an endpoint
statements.conclusion: t<=(sqrt(n)-1)/(sqrt(n)+1). Equality holds precisely, up to simultaneous row/column permutation, for A_*=(n-1)^(-1) sum_{i<n} ell_i^T ell_i, ell_i=(1-1/sqrt(n))e_i+(1/sqrt(n))e_n; extremal symmetry is forced.
hypotheses: A is a real entrywise nonnegative n by n matrix with rank(A)<n, total entry sum one, and PAP=(t/n)P.
No symmetry or positive-semidefiniteness of A is assumed.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: lem:r75-singular-coefficient
statements.limits: The stated dimension restriction n>=5 is used in strict equality separation; no extension of this uniqueness assertion to n<=4 is claimed. The lemma does not assume or classify a chosen hidden implementation.
statements.proof: A normalized left null vector gives A=(t/n)(I+c1^T-1v^T), v.c=0 and sum(c)=1/t. Entrywise positivity yields lower bounds controlled by the largest, second largest and most negative v coordinates. A strictly concave one-variable bound reduces to two endpoints; AM-GM gives the sharp constant. Equality forces one negative null coordinate and a unique slack support, hence A_*. Orthogonal centered probability rows prove attainment.

statements.claim_class: Exact all-contrast resource law, matching constructions and endpoint rigidity for an unbounded nonabelian family. The rational low-contrast and full-contrast arguments are retained as additional explicit results.
classical_ingredients: Standard representation of S_n and character orthogonality
statements.conclusion: For t>0, observable group S_n, residual count n!, dimension 1+(n-1)^2 and module bound n(n-1). With tau=(sqrt(n)-1)/(sqrt(n)+1), kappa is n(n-1) on 0<t<=tau and n^2 above; pure memory adds one. At tau every minimum core has n-1 natural orbits and precisely the stated ell_i preparations and D_i=ell_i/((n-1)w_i), with sum(w_i)=1 and w_i>=(1-1/sqrt(n))/(n-1). At t=0 both minima are one.
hypotheses: n>=5 and binary S_n response beta_t(g)=(1-t)/n+t*chi_n(g)/n for 0<=t<=1.
For positive contrast, arbitrary finite exact stochastic controllers under the retained prepared-response interface; all finite G-set orbit types are permitted in the positive-core reduction.
The equality classification concerns minimum permutation cores at the attained threshold, not all unreduced stochastic implementations.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: thm:r75-symmetric-return
statements.limits: The equality classification stops at the permutation-core level. The two-command prepared quantum realization proves physical availability, not minimal Hilbert dimension or a common-resource quantum advantage. The relative gap tends to one. No A1/A2 or full Theta-pipeline completion follows.
statements.proof: The full standard Fourier block fixes the observable invariants. Counting natural point-orbits of every subgroup gives the unrestricted index lower and a strict penalty for nonnatural standard carriers. Any core below n^2 therefore has exactly n-1 natural carriers; all extra-orbit contributions are constant and can be absorbed into their decoders. Its coefficient matrix is nonnegative singular with PAP=(t/n)P, so the sharp lemma gives the exact lower. A_* gives the threshold controller and decoder mixing all smaller contrasts; n natural return orbits give the upper above threshold. Nonnegative rank-one support/ratio rigidity classifies every minimum threshold factorization. The retained pure-start formula completes the count.

statements.claim_class: A general exact relation between two initialization conventions in the classical positive-realization framework; neither that framework nor stationarity itself is newly claimed.
classical_ingredients: Cesaro averaging of finite stochastic matrices
statements.conclusion: The minima are both one for a one-label response, and otherwise n_pure=n_mix+1, with infinity+1=infinity. A stationary hidden row for the averaged command can be chosen without enlarging a mixed realization.
hypotheses: A nonempty finite command alphabet with finite report sets and an observable response predictively stationary under a full-support command mixture.
All future-word stationarity equalities are required; when terminal decoders are part of the experiment, all word/readout identities include the empty word.
Mixed and pure minima use arbitrary real nonnegative edge-emitting tables, with a prescribed pure initial label counted; no irreducibility or minimal linear-state assumption.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: thm:r75-stationary-initializer
statements.limits: Full-support observable stationarity and all terminal quantifiers are material. This is an edge-emitting process theorem. External policy memory, coefficient bit length and exact sampling cost are separate.
statements.proof: Predictive stationarity writes the initial future function as a convex combination of hidden future functions. Unless the one-label exception holds, eliminate the initial label and redirect every transition into it using the same normalized coefficients; induction includes zero-length terminal readout. Conversely one counted initializer executes the first actual command into any mixed core. Cesaro averaging preserves every future response and supplies a stationary averaged-command hidden row.

statements.conclusion: The minimum pure-start HMM has exactly one more label than the minimum mixed-start HMM, with the infinite-value convention.

Edge-emitting HMM realizations, with freely mixed initialization compared to a counted prescribed pure label.

statements.limits: Not a new solution of the unrestricted minimum positive-state realization problem, and not a claim for a different state-emitting model convention.

statements.claim_class: Physical and rank verification for this complete damped family, extending the retained undamped example. Low-rank non-HMM phase mechanisms and one-dependent examples have prior antecedents.
statements.conclusion: All branches are completely positive with the displayed report floors, sum exactly to depolarization, and give fixed-command stationarity and one-dependence. The explicit cylinder has three independent modes and predictive rank three at nonreal positive retention, and rank two at zero retention; the response is never one-label.
hypotheses: The displayed complete three-report qubit instrument, retention parameter 0<=alpha<=1 and any real angle theta; initial state I/2.
For rank three, alpha>0 and sin(theta)!=0; the zero-retention endpoint is handled separately.

statements.label: lem:r75-noisy-physical
statements.limits: Fixed-command stationarity and one-dependence are not claims about feedback-controlled records. The pure-reset branch violates the R68 every-posterior interior hypothesis at every block length, so that theorem is not being applied here.
statements.proof: Choi-matrix norm bounds give a positive I/16 margin for the complement branch. The rank-one report resets to tau, allowing direct iteration of the damped rotation and the cylinder formula. A nonzero Vandermonde minor gives rank three; the zero-retention two-by-two Hankel minor gives rank two, with a matching two-dimensional reachable diagonal space.

statements.claim_class: A matched necessary spectral obstruction and sufficient complete-instrument construction; the relative-spectrum mechanism is inherited and its reducible-core proof is explicitly carried through here.
classical_ingredients: Perron-Frobenius normalization on one irreducible block
Invariant physical-state dictionaries and barycentric interpolation
statements.conclusion: Every M-label mixed realization forces alpha*exp(i*theta) into the M-state stochastic eigenvalue region. Conversely the polygon supplies an exact q-label realization of all report branches, word states, terminal POVMs and common adaptive policies, using one dictionary for all eligible commands.
hypotheses: The complete instrument of the preceding lemma; alpha>0 and sin(theta)!=0 for the arbitrary-HMM lower.
For the upper, a regular q-gon of actual pure qubit states, q>=3, with a reset vertex and alpha*exp(i*theta) in that polygon; the same condition may hold for a whole command family.

statements.label: lem:r75-full-instrument-bounds
statements.limits: The entire stochastic eigenvalue region is only a necessary condition, not proved sufficient for arbitrary full instruments. The upper is restricted to the actual invariant polygon and its qualifying angle family.
statements.proof: Positive entrance/exit paths bound the productive zero-report core by C*8^(-n). Cayley-Hamilton forces the observed nonreal eigenvalue into a productive irreducible block; Perron normalization there and a stationary-row contraction yield the exact normalized stochastic eigenvalue. For the upper, branch zero preserves the polygon, branch one resets to its vertex and branch two has normalized Bloch norm at most 5/11, inside every eligible polygon. Barycentric branch interpolation proves the full subnormalized-state identities.

statements.claim_class: Exact complete-instrument and simultaneous-command realization results using inherited spectral geometry. The sector curve and inverse-square-root worst-phase exponent are not claimed as new classical spectral discoveries.
classical_ingredients: Classical stochastic sector inequality and boundary equality case
statements.conclusion: Exact first-sector mixed feasibility alpha<=1/(cos(theta)+sin(theta)tan(pi/M)), with exact M/M+1 counts and zero-report lazy-cycle Perron rigidity at equality. The simultaneous all-angle mixed optimum is K=max(3,ceil(pi/arccos(alpha))), with pure optimum K+1. At alpha=0 the counts are 2/3; at alpha=1 the full family is infinite, with inherited fixed-phase finite/infinite alternatives.
hypotheses: The displayed complete noisy qubit instrument; first sector M>=3, 0<theta<=2*pi/M, 0<alpha<=1.
For the common all-angle count, 0<alpha<1; a finite alphabet has the same upper and a matching lower when it contains a worst phase.
Pure-start counts use the stationary-response theorem; zero-retention and undamped endpoints are stated separately.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: thm:r75-noisy-memory
statements.limits: Rigidity is for the zero-report matrix up to diagonal similarity, cyclic relabeling and orientation; the other branches are not uniquely classified. No full fixed-angle formula outside the proved regimes is claimed. The R71 arithmetic lift is inherited reasoning, not a new number-theoretic theorem.
statements.proof: The necessary spectrum and actual polygon upper meet on the classical first-sector chord. Strict smaller-size sector exclusion forces the full carrying block, and applying the sector bound before radial contraction fixes its Perron root at 1/8 and the normalized lazy cycle. A polygon containing the whole radius-alpha disk gives one all-command dictionary; one critical phase gives its matching lower. Explicit two-state rational branch tables settle zero retention. The general initializer theorem gives every pure charge.

statements.claim_class: A uniform bounded-target-cost implementation upper for the complete controlled stopped experiment, with a counted memory construction; not a new generic telescoping principle.
classical_ingredients: Trace-norm contraction of positive trace-preserving maps on Hermitian inputs
Tail-sum formula for expected stopping time
statements.conclusion: Uniform complete stopped-law total variation, including the nontermination atom, is at most epsilon*B/8. The stronger terminal classical-quantum trace-distance estimate holds with a scalar nontermination block. Pure memory at tolerance delta is at most 1+max(3,ceil(pi/arccos(1-8*delta/B)))=(pi/4)*sqrt(B/delta)+O(1) in the stated regime; an L-label policy adds the explicit product-core account.
hypotheses: A finite angle command alphabet, initial qubit I/2 and target retention alpha=1.
One class of common randomized command/stopping/terminal-POVM policies, each with target expected calls E_1^pi(tau)<=B<infinity; no external quantum register entangled with the qubit.
One approximate model with retention 1-epsilon, 0<epsilon<1, is chosen independently of the policy; the epsilon=1 and B=0 cases are explicit.
statements.identity: R75 numbered addition; count does not imply mathematical novelty or journal endorsement.
statements.label: thm:r75-stopped-approximation
statements.limits: The budget is under the target, not the approximation. The latter may have nontermination mass and unbounded expected cost. No matching approximation lower or optimal exponent is proved, and the one-call constant excludes an entangled external quantum register.
statements.proof: The two opposite branch perturbations have one-call flagged trace distance at most epsilon*tr(X)/8 for a positive single-qubit input. Finite-horizon telescoping keeps every changed-call prefix entirely target, weighting error by target survival probabilities. Common positive trace-preserving tails contract the difference. Retaining all finite stopped blocks and merging unfinished histories into a scalar block yields the infinite-horizon limit, including nontermination. The exact noisy dictionary and initializer provide the memory upper.
